input.question: What were the last places in the world to outlaw slavery and when did they abolish the practice?
input.ground_truth: I hope this qualifies as a top level comment, but, there are still places where Slavery's illegal status is unenforced. [Mauritania](_URL_0_) had a pretty high-profile article written on it last year. Technically it abolished Slavery in 1981, and made it illegal in 2007, though last year's report indicates that that it is still occuring there with regularity.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: What were the last places in the world to outlaw slavery and when did they abolish the practice?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine the whole world is a big playground. Most kids in the playground stopped playing a mean game called “slavery” a long, long time ago. But some kids kept playing it for a while.

The very last place to stop playing that mean game was a country called Mauritania. They stopped in the year 1981. But even after that, some people there still played that mean game secretly for many, many more years.

So, the last country to officially say “No more slavery!” was Mauritania, in 1981. But it took even longer for everyone to really stop doing it.
